intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square at Dusk
experiences.description: Experience the legendary main square of Marrakech as it transforms at sunset into a spectacular open-air theatre. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform while sampling freshly squeezed orange juice and traditional Moroccan street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and grilled merguez sausages from the famous food stalls.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, arriving at a traditional Berber nomad camp for an unforgettable night under a sky blazing with stars. Enjoy a tagine dinner cooked over an open fire, listen to Gnawa drumming and music around the campfire, and wake at dawn to witness the sunrise paint the dunes in shades of amber and rose.

experiences.name: Medina Souks & Tanneries Walking Tour
experiences.description: Hire a local guide to navigate the labyrinthine medieval souks of Marrakech, exploring the ancient leather tanneries of the Chouara district where hides are still dyed using centuries-old methods. Visit the spice souk, the lantern makers, and the carpet weavers while learning about the history of trade along the trans-Saharan caravan routes that made Marrakech a legendary imperial city.
experiences.location: Northern Medina Souks & Chouara Tannery, Marrakech

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local Marrakchi family or a riad-based chef for a hands-on cooking class beginning with a guided tour of the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare authentic dishes including chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, and honey-drenched chebakia pastries, gaining deep insight into the Berber, Arab, and Andalusian culinary heritage that defines Moroccan cuisine.

experiences.name: Aït Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Exploration
experiences.description: Take a day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Aït Benhaddou, a breathtaking fortified mud-brick village that has served as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue through the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, stopping at ancient kasbahs, Berber villages, and date palm oases while a local guide shares the rich history of the Glaoui dynasty and trans-Saharan trade.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the airport bus (Line 19, ~20 MAD / ~$2) or a petit taxi (negotiate to ~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a quick msemen (Moroccan flatbread) or harira soup from a late-night street stall near Jemaa el-Fna (~10–15 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) ready before leaving the airport – exchange a small amount at the airport bureau de change. The hotel is a short walk or taxi ride from Jemaa el-Fna square. Don't over-negotiate late at night; agree on a fair price and rest up.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at a café near the hotel – mint tea, msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), and hard-boiled eggs (~20–30 MAD). Then walk to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (free to view from outside) and stroll through the souks of the Medina. Explore the spice market (Rahba Kedima) and the dyers' souk. Bargain respectfully – it's part of the culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD / ~$7) – a stunning 19th-century riad palace with intricate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, head to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the old Jewish cemetery for a quiet, reflective walk. Stop by the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD) – a beautifully decorated royal necropolis from the 16th century.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jemaa el-Fna square as the sun sets – watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians for free. Eat dinner at the famous open-air food stalls in the square (stall numbers 1–30 are popular). Try harira soup (~10 MAD), merguez sandwiches (~15 MAD), and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~4 MAD). Total dinner budget: ~50–70 MAD.

meals.breakfast: Café near hotel – mint tea, msemen, amlou (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant in the Medina – tagine or couscous set menu (~40–60 MAD). Try Restaurant Haj Boujemaa near the souks.
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – harira, merguez, orange juice (~50–70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina's narrow alleys are uneven. Keep your bag close in crowded areas. Most palaces and tombs open around 9:00 AM. Friday afternoons may have limited access to some sites due to prayers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (~70 MAD) – one of the most beautiful Islamic schools in North Africa, featuring stunning zellige tilework and carved stucco. Nearby, explore the Museum of Marrakech (~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace. Then wander through the northern Medina souks – leather goods, lanterns, and textiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi or walk (~20 min) to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum area. The garden itself costs ~150 MAD, but if budget is tight, admire the cobalt-blue walls from outside and explore the surrounding Gueliz neighborhood (the French New Town). Walk along Avenue Mohammed V for a contrast between old and new Marrakech. Visit a local hammam for an authentic scrub experience – try Hammam Dar el-Bacha (~50–80 MAD for basic entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina for dinner. Try a local 'restaurant du peuple' (workers' restaurant) near Bab Doukkala for an authentic, ultra-cheap meal – a full plate of couscous or tagine with bread costs ~25–35 MAD. Afterward, enjoy a free evening walk through the lit-up Medina alleys and pick up some local pastries (chebakia, ghriba) from a bakery (~5–10 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café – coffee and Moroccan pancakes (baghrir) (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food near Ben Youssef – kefta sandwich or bissara (fava bean soup) with bread (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local workers' restaurant near Bab Doukkala – tagine or couscous (~30–40 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is a must-see – arrive early (before 10 AM) to avoid crowds. Hammams are gender-separated; ask the hotel for the best local hammam recommendation. Gueliz is great for budget supermarkets if you need snacks or water for the upcoming desert trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at 6:00–7:00 AM. Join a shared budget group tour to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi) – book through your hotel or a local agency in Jemaa el-Fna. Shared 3-day/2-night tours cost approximately 900–1,200 MAD (~$90–120) per person and include transport, accommodation, and camel ride. The drive passes through the stunning Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at Aït Benhaddou – a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in Game of Thrones and Gladiator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley – a lush palm oasis cutting through dramatic desert landscapes. Stop in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') for lunch and a quick look at the Taourirt Kasbah (exterior free, interior ~20 MAD). Continue east through Skoura and the Valley of Roses toward the desert.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga by late afternoon/early evening. Mount camels for a 1-hour sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes – one of the most magical experiences in Morocco. Arrive at a desert camp (included in tour), enjoy a traditional Berber dinner (tagine, bread, mint tea) around a campfire, and listen to Gnawa music under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or packed snack before departure (~20 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate – set menu tagine (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp – traditional Berber tagine and mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Book the shared Sahara tour 1–2 days in advance from Jemaa el-Fna agencies or your hotel. Compare at least 3 prices. The drive is long (~9–10 hours total) but incredibly scenic. Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes for a breathtaking sunrise over the Sahara – one of the most unforgettable moments of the trip (free, included in camp stay). Take photos, meditate, or simply absorb the silence. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast – bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, and mint tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Merzouga village on foot or by rented bicycle (~30–50 MAD/hour). Visit the local Gnawa musicians' quarter and the small lake (Dayet Srji) nearby, which attracts flamingos in spring. Optionally, visit a fossil and mineral shop – the region is famous for trilobite fossils (bargain hard, starting prices are inflated). Begin the return journey toward Marrakech in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stop in the Todra Gorge or Dades Valley if the tour route allows – dramatic canyon landscapes perfect for a short walk. Continue driving back toward Marrakech. Arrive late evening (~21:00–22:00). Grab a quick bite near the hotel – a bowl of harira and bread from a street vendor (~15 MAD) and rest.

meals.breakfast: Included in desert camp – Berber breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop en route (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Street food near hotel on return – harira soup and bread (~15–20 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is equally scenic. If your tour includes a stop at Todra Gorge, take it – it's spectacular and free to walk through. Stay hydrated throughout the day. Keep your camera accessible for the sunrise – it's worth every early-morning effort.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the long desert journey. Sleep in, then enjoy a leisurely Moroccan breakfast at a rooftop café near Jemaa el-Fna with views of the Koutoubia Mosque (~30–40 MAD). Afterward, revisit any souks you didn't fully explore and do last-minute souvenir shopping – argan oil, leather goods, spices, and Berber rugs. Bargain confidently: start at 30–40% of the asking price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD) – a 16th-century palace destroyed by the Alaouite sultan, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls. Explore the Mellah market for cheap local produce and snacks. Then visit the Tanneries of Marrakech (free to view from leather shop terraces – a small tip of ~10–20 MAD is appreciated) for a colorful and pungent look at traditional leather dyeing.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on your last full evening dinner – try a mid-range local restaurant like Café des Épices or a riad restaurant for a proper Moroccan feast (pastilla, tagine, bastilla au lait dessert) for ~100–150 MAD. Afterward, enjoy one final walk through Jemaa el-Fna, watch the acrobats and musicians, and sip fresh orange juice as a farewell to Marrakech.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop café near Jemaa el-Fna – mint tea, msemen, eggs (~35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Souk street food – kefta wrap, olives, and fresh juice (~30–40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge at a local riad restaurant – pastilla and tagine (~120–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a busy market day – the souks will be lively and full. This is your best day for souvenir shopping. For argan oil, buy from a women's cooperative for fair-trade authenticity. Avoid touts who offer 'free' tours of the tanneries – they will pressure you to buy.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Take a peaceful early walk through the Medina before the crowds arrive – the alleys are magical in the morning light. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens one last time for a quiet moment. Pick up any last items – a bag of Moroccan spice mix (ras el hanout) or a small ceramic tagine as a gift (~20–50 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, check out of Hotel Aday (standard checkout is 12:00 noon – ask about late checkout if needed). Store luggage at the hotel if your flight is later. Take a final mint tea at a café, review your memories, and head to Marrakech Menara Airport. Take the airport bus Line 19 (~20 MAD) or a petit taxi (~80–100 MAD negotiated).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech. Carry snacks from the Medina for the journey – dates, dried figs, and almond cookies are perfect travel food and cost ~20–30 MAD for a generous bag.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast – café near hotel, mint tea and msemen (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch before departure – sandwich or bowl of harira (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before your flight. Marrakech Menara Airport is small but can get busy on weekends. Declare any argan oil over 100ml in checked luggage. Keep a small amount of MAD for the taxi or bus to the airport. Total estimated 7-day budget (excluding flights and tour): approximately 2,500–3,500 MAD (~$250–350 USD) per person.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Hotel Aday in the Medina, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in-flight or transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport taxi or ride-share (~150–200 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat. Check in, unwind with mint tea if offered by the riad, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store in the Medina, or ask the hotel if a late snack is available.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival logistics simple. Confirm your taxi or transfer in advance. The Medina's narrow alleys can be tricky at night — ask the hotel to send GPS coordinates or meet you at a nearby landmark like Jemaa el-Fna square.

day_by_day.morning: After a restful sleep, enjoy breakfast at the hotel. Then walk to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-minute walk) to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, locals heading to work, and the buzz of the Medina waking up. Head into the souks (Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices) for a 2-hour self-guided exploration of spices, leather goods, ceramics, and textiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (15-minute walk from the hotel, ~70 MAD entry) — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate tilework and lush gardens. Afterward, explore the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD entry), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis from the 16th century.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at dusk to witness the square transform into a vibrant open-air spectacle — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Stroll the perimeter and take it all in before dinner.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday — most riads include a traditional Moroccan breakfast (msemen flatbread, honey, argan oil, olives, mint tea).
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near Place Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace with great views, tagines and salads for ~80–120 MAD per person.
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — try harira soup, merguez sausages, and kefta skewers for an authentic and affordable experience (~60–100 MAD). Alternatively, Restaurant Chez Lamine for slow-cooked mechoui lamb (~150 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small amount of cash (MAD) handy for entry fees and food stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims) and the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry) — a 16th-century palace with sweeping views from the ramparts and resident storks nesting on the walls. Then head to the Maison de la Photographie or the Museum of Moroccan Arts (Dar Si Said, ~30 MAD) for cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (~150 MAD combined entry) — a vivid cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, now one of Marrakech's most photographed spots. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the exotic plants, Berber museum, and the adjacent YSL memorial garden.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the Medina for a relaxed evening. Explore the quieter northern souks (Souk Haddadine — the blacksmiths' souk) and browse artisan workshops. End the evening with a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range public hammam near the Medina (~150–250 MAD for a full scrub and massage).

meals.breakfast: At the hotel.
meals.lunch: Café Kif Kif near the Majorelle Garden area — colorful, vegetarian-friendly café with Moroccan salads and wraps (~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: Le Foundouk restaurant in the northern Medina — beautifully restored caravanserai with Moroccan-French fusion cuisine; tagines and pastilla (~200–300 MAD per person, mid-range splurge).

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance — it sells out, especially in spring. The hammam is a must-do cultural experience; ask the hotel to recommend a reputable local one rather than a tourist-oriented spa.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert — join a shared or private day-tour to the Draa Valley and Zagora, OR opt for the more popular 2-day/1-night Merzouga (Erg Chebbi) excursion. For a 7-day trip, a private overnight Merzouga tour (departing today, returning tomorrow evening) is highly recommended. The drive takes ~8–9 hours via the High Atlas Mountains and Draa Valley — scenery is spectacular. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive through the Atlas Mountains, passing through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') — stop briefly at the Kasbah Taourirt (~30 MAD entry), a stunning earthen fortress. Continue southeast through the Valley of Roses (Dades Valley) and the dramatic Draa Valley palm groves.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga (~18:00–19:00). Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset ride into the dunes to your desert camp. Watch the sun set over the Sahara — one of Morocco's most breathtaking experiences. Enjoy a Berber dinner under the stars with live drumming and music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack snacks for the road.
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate or a stop along the route — traditional tagine set menu (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Included at the desert camp — traditional Berber meal: harira, tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable tour operator in advance (e.g., Sahara Expedition, Desert Majesty, or through your hotel). Mid-range overnight desert camp costs ~600–900 MAD per person including camel ride, dinner, breakfast, and a private or semi-private tent. March weather in the Sahara is ideal — warm days (~25°C), cool nights (~10°C). Bring a light jacket, sunscreen, and a headscarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) for a magical Sahara sunrise over the dunes — one of the most memorable moments of the trip. Take a short walk or sandboard on the dunes. Enjoy a simple breakfast at the camp (mint tea, bread, honey, eggs). Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different route through the Todra Gorge — a dramatic 300m-high canyon carved by the Todra River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Todra Gorge for a 1-hour walk through the narrow canyon (free entry). Continue west through the Dades Gorge (the 'Road of a Thousand Kasbahs') — stop at a roadside café for lunch and admire the dramatic rock formations. Continue driving back toward Marrakech through the High Atlas.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech (~19:00–20:00). Check back into Hotel Aday, shower, and decompress. Take a gentle evening stroll around Jemaa el-Fna for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included at the desert camp.
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant in the Dades Valley — fresh salads, tagine, and fresh-squeezed juice (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant near Place des Épices in Marrakech — modern Moroccan cuisine on a rooftop terrace with Medina views; lamb pastilla or vegetable couscous (~180–250 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is long (~8–9 hours with stops). Bring water, snacks, and a good playlist or podcast. The Todra Gorge is best visited in the morning light. If energy allows, a short evening walk to Jemaa el-Fna is a great way to re-immerse in city life after the desert.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient Roman ruins of Volubilis and the holy city of Moulay Idriss — OR, if you prefer to stay closer to Marrakech, take a half-day excursion to the Ourika Valley in the Atlas Mountains (45 minutes from Marrakech). The Ourika Valley offers Berber villages, a waterfall hike, and stunning mountain scenery. Visit a local argan oil cooperative run by Berber women for a free demonstration and fair-trade shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Marrakech by early afternoon. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (housed in a stunning 19th-century palace, ~50 MAD) for Moroccan art and historical artifacts. Spend the remaining afternoon doing any last-minute souk shopping — pick up saffron, argan oil, leather goods, or handwoven textiles as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge on a special farewell dinner at a traditional Moroccan riad restaurant. Enjoy a full Moroccan feast: pastilla (pigeon or chicken pie), lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, couscous, and chebakia (honey pastry) for dessert — all served in an atmospheric candlelit courtyard.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel.
meals.lunch: In the Ourika Valley — a simple Berber lunch at a family-run mountain restaurant with panoramic views (~80–120 MAD); or a quick lunch at a Medina café upon return.
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout or Riad Dar Zitoun — iconic Marrakech riad dining experience with live Gnawa music; budget ~300–400 MAD per person for a full set menu (a worthwhile splurge for the final evening).

day_by_day.notes: The Ourika Valley excursion can be done by shared taxi (grand taxi) from Bab Rob gate for ~50–80 MAD each way, or via a guided half-day tour (~300–500 MAD). Saturday is market day in some Atlas villages — a great opportunity to see local Berber commerce. Book the riad dinner in advance as popular spots fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take one last slow walk through the Medina to revisit your favorite spots: the spice souk, a rooftop café for mint tea, or the peaceful Koutoubia gardens. Visit any remaining sights you may have missed — the Almoravid Koubba (the oldest surviving monument in Marrakech, ~20 MAD) is a hidden gem near the Musée de Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, use the afternoon for final packing, souvenir shopping, or a relaxed café stop. Check out of Hotel Aday and arrange a taxi to the airport. Marrakech Menara Airport is about 15–20 minutes from the Medina (~100–150 MAD by taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Marrakech Menara Airport. Carry memories of the Medina's labyrinthine souks, the golden Sahara dunes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at the hotel — savor the mint tea, msemen, and honey one last time.
meals.lunch: Café du Grand Balcon overlooking Jemaa el-Fna — a classic Marrakech institution with great views and simple Moroccan fare (~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: At the airport or on the plane.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some MAD for the taxi and any last-minute purchases. Duty-free at Marrakech airport has a decent selection of Moroccan argan products and spices if you run out of time to shop in the Medina.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Private airport transfer arranged with a luxury chauffeur service to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony and a light late-night snack prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival (22:30). Check in to Hotel Aday, freshen up, and enjoy the hotel's curated welcome amenities — traditional pastries, argan oil toiletries, and a chilled bottle of Moroccan rosé or fresh juice. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome spread at Hotel Aday — Moroccan mezze, harira soup, msemen flatbread, and seasonal fruit arranged by the hotel upon request

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Hotel Aday. Keep Day 1 light — no sightseeing. The Medina streets near Derb Sidi Bouloukat can be narrow; ensure the driver knows the closest vehicle drop-off point.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast on the hotel's rooftop terrace. At 10:00, begin a private guided walking tour of the Marrakech Medina — explore the historic Mouassine Quarter, the ornate Ben Youssef Madrasa (one of North Africa's largest Islamic colleges), and the ancient Almoravid Koubba. Your private guide will provide rich historical context about the city's 11th-century origins.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, visit the Bahia Palace (Palais de la Bahia) — a stunning 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture with intricately carved cedarwood ceilings and mosaic courtyards. Follow with a curated visit to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the historic Saadian Tombs, lavishly decorated royal mausoleums dating to the 16th century. End the afternoon with a private session at a premium tannery viewing gallery to witness the ancient leather-dyeing craft.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk to absorb the spectacle of storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the square for a dramatic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday — Moroccan pancakes (baghrir), honey, amlou (argan-almond spread), fresh orange juice, mint tea, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, near the Spice Market) — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with stunning Medina rooftop views; try the lamb pastilla and roasted vegetable couscous
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin (32 Souk Jeld, Sidi Abdelaziz) — an elegant garden restaurant set in a lush riad courtyard; signature dishes include slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon and saffron chicken bastilla

day_by_day.notes: Book Ben Youssef Madrasa tickets in advance — it is one of Marrakech's most visited sites. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina's cobblestone streets. A private licensed guide is strongly recommended for historical depth and navigating the souks.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart at 09:00 for a private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech). The cobalt-blue Majorelle Garden, restored by YSL and Pierre Bergé, is a botanical masterpiece. The museum showcases the designer's deep love affair with Morocco and his iconic collections. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Medina for an immersive private cooking class at a premium riad kitchen. Learn to prepare classic Moroccan dishes — harira soup, chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, and orange-blossom pastilla. This hands-on 3-hour class with a master chef is both educational and deeply cultural.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam and spa evening at a luxury traditional hammam — book a private session at Hammam de la Rose or Heritage Spa near the Medina. Enjoy a black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return to the hotel refreshed for a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday — eggs kefta, msemen with honey and butter, fresh-squeezed orange juice, mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café Kif Kif (near Majorelle) or a curated picnic basket prepared by the hotel to enjoy in the Majorelle Garden grounds
meals.dinner: Private dinner at your cooking class riad — enjoy the dishes you prepared, served in a candlelit courtyard with Moroccan wine or fresh-pressed pomegranate juice

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum tickets online well in advance — they sell out frequently. The cooking class should be pre-booked through the hotel concierge. Hammam sessions should also be reserved ahead of time for a private experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:30 by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the epic journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The route crosses the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) — one of Morocco's most scenic mountain roads. Stop at the Kasbah Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and legendary film location (Gladiator, Game of Thrones). Explore the ancient fortified village with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley and the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses), stopping at Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios. Continue east through dramatic desert landscapes, kasbahs, and palm oases toward Merzouga.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga at approximately 18:00–19:00. Mount private camels (or opt for a 4x4 dune buggy) for a sunset ride into the Sahara. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp — a premium tented camp with en-suite facilities, Persian rugs, and lantern lighting. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under a sky blazing with stars, accompanied by live Gnawa music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure — packed to-go option available
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Ouarzazate — Chez Dimitri or the restaurant at Berbère Palace Hotel; enjoy Moroccan salads, lamb brochettes, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast at the luxury desert camp — slow-cooked lamb mechoui, vegetable couscous, Moroccan salads, fresh dates, and mint tea; optional Moroccan wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~8–9 hours total with stops). Depart early. Ensure the private driver is experienced on mountain roads. The luxury desert camp should be pre-booked — recommended options include Luxury Camp Erg Chebbi or Scarabeo Camp. Bring a warm layer — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private sunrise camel or 4x4 ride to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of the most breathtaking experiences in North Africa. Watch the Sahara ignite in gold and amber as the sun rises over the dunes. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a guided walk with a Berber nomad to learn about desert survival and traditional life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the desert camp and visit the village of Merzouga — explore the local Berber market, visit a fossil and mineral artisan workshop (the region is famous for ancient marine fossils), and stop at a traditional Berber family home for tea and conversation. Begin the return journey westward, stopping at the Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300-meter-high rose-red cliffs, ideal for a scenic walk along the river.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to your overnight luxury riad in Tinghir or Boumalne Dades — a beautifully restored kasbah-style property in the Dades Valley. Enjoy a quiet evening with a private terrace dinner overlooking the valley.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the desert camp — Berber bread, honey, olive oil, eggs, fresh fruit, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Todra Gorge — fresh trout from the gorge river, Moroccan salads, and tagine
meals.dinner: Private dinner at your luxury riad in Tinghir/Dades Valley — slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, Moroccan pastilla, and seasonal desserts

day_by_day.notes: Set an alarm for 05:00 to catch the sunrise — it is the highlight of the desert experience. The Todra Gorge walk is easy and suitable for all fitness levels. Confirm your riad booking in the Dades/Tinghir area in advance.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, explore the Dades Gorge (Gorges du Dadès) — a dramatic canyon carved by the Dades River, lined with ancient kasbahs and almond trees in bloom (March is peak blossom season). Take a scenic drive through the 'Road of a Thousand Kasbahs' with your private driver, stopping at photogenic fortified villages and viewpoints. Visit the Roses Valley (Vallée des Roses) near El Kelaa M'Gouna, famous for its Damask rose cultivation — in mid-March the roses are beginning to bloom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the return journey toward Marrakech via the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Stop at a premium argan oil cooperative near Aït Ourir for a guided tour and tasting — learn how Berber women produce argan oil and purchase authentic products directly from the source. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon (approximately 17:00–18:00).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Aday. Freshen up and head out for a final evening in the Marrakech Medina — browse the premium artisan souks for last-minute curated souvenirs (handwoven carpets, silver jewelry, leather goods). Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your Dades Valley riad — fresh bread, local honey, Berber omelette, mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch at a scenic stop in the High Atlas — packed gourmet lunch box prepared by the riad, or a stop at a local mountain restaurant for harira and tagine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dar Yacout (79 Sidi Ahmed Soussi, Marrakech) — one of Marrakech's most iconic luxury dining experiences; a multi-course feast in a stunning 17th-century riad with rooftop views, live Andalusian music, and dishes including bastilla, mechoui lamb, and honey-drenched pastries

day_by_day.notes: Book Dar Yacout well in advance — it is one of Marrakech's most sought-after dinner reservations. The argan cooperative visit is a meaningful cultural and ethical shopping experience. March almond and rose blossoms in the Dades Valley make this route particularly scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins — a 16th-century Saadian palace once described as one of the wonders of the world, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on its towers. Explore the on-site museum housing the original minbar (pulpit) from the Koutoubia Mosque. Walk to the iconic Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful stroll and photos of the 12th-century minaret.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souk exploration — visit the premium artisan district near the Mouassine Fountain for high-quality Moroccan crafts: hand-painted ceramics, bespoke leather bags, silver Berber jewelry, and handwoven kilim rugs. Stop for a final mint tea at a traditional café. Return to the hotel for luggage collection and check-out. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary week spanning imperial Medinas, High Atlas mountain passes, ancient kasbahs, and the infinite silence of the Sahara.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at Hotel Aday — full spread of Moroccan pastries, fresh orange juice, eggs, mint tea, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Café des Épices (75 Rahba Lakdima, Place des Épices) — a beloved Medina rooftop café with panoramic spice market views; enjoy Moroccan wraps, zaalouk, and fresh lemonade with rose water
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — alternatively, a light early dinner at the airport lounge or a quick stop at a premium café near the hotel before transfer

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy on Sundays. Consider purchasing a curated gift box of Moroccan spices, argan oil, and rose water from a reputable Medina shop as a final souvenir. Confirm private airport transfer the night before.
